filings.text: EX-99.1 2 exh_991.htm PRESS RELEASE EXHIBIT 99.1 Nutanix Reports First Quarter Fiscal 2027 Financial Results Reports 15% YoY ARR Growth and Solid Free Cash Flow Nutanix Announces CEO Succession Plan; Board Initiates Search for Next CEO SAN JOSE, Calif., Nov. 24, 2026 (GLOBE NEWSWIRE) -- Nutanix, Inc. (NASDAQ: NTNX), a hybrid cloud leader and AI platform company, today announced financial results for its first quarter ended October 31, 2026. “In the first quarter we delivered results that exceeded all of our guided metrics,” said Rajiv Ramaswami, CEO of Nutanix. “We also continued to invest in our cloud platform, especially with respect to AI and broadening our support for external storage.” “Our first quarter results demonstrated a good balance of top and bottom line performance with 15% year-over-year ARR growth and solid free cash flow generation,” said Rukmini Sivaraman, CFO of Nutanix. “We remain focused on delivering sustainable growth and improving profitability.” Nutanix today separately announced that the Board is working with Chief Executive Officer Rajiv Ramaswami to identify and recruit his successor, and he will step down after his successor has been appointed and assumes the role. Ramaswami will continue to serve as a senior advisor to the Company for a period of time after his successor is in place to ensure a smooth transition. The Board has engaged a leading national search firm to assist the process of identifying Nutanix’s next CEO. For the nine months ended October 31, 2026, revenue was $323.7 million, up 11.7% from $289.8 million for the nine months ended October 31, 2025. • Gross margin under U.S. generally accepted accounting principles (GAAP) for the third quarter of fiscal 2027 was 57.8%, compared with 59.6% for the same period in fiscal 2026. Financial results on a non-GAAP basis for the third quarter of fiscal 2027 are as follows: • Gross margin on a non-GAAP basis for the third quarter of fiscal 2027 was 59.5%, compared with 60.9% for the same period in fiscal 2026. For the nine months ended October 31, 2026, non-GAAP gross margin was 59.6%, compared with 61.1% for the nine months ended October 31, 2025. • Non-GAAP net income for the third quarter of fiscal 2027 was $12.7 million, or earnings per diluted ordinary share of $0.28. Ambarella reports gross margin, net income (loss) and earnings (losses) per share in accordance with GAAP and, additionally, on a non-GAAP basis. Non-GAAP financial information excludes the impact of stock-based compensation, nonrecurring development project termination credit and acquisition- related costs adjusted for the associated tax impact, which includes the effect of any benefits or shortfalls recognized. A reconciliation of the GAAP to non-GAAP gross margin, net income (loss) and earnings (losses) per share for the periods presented, as well as a description of the items excluded from the non-GAAP calculations, is included in the financial statements portion of this press release. Physical AI brings domain specific context to LLMs running in the datacenter, which differentiates and improves the overall combined edge AI and cloud AI value proposition. A live and archived webcast of the call will be available on Ambarella’s website at http://www.ambarella.com/ for up to 30 days after the call. About Ambarella With an installed base of more than 55 million AI SoC units, Ambarella’s products are utilized in a wide variety of physical edge AI applications, spanning edge endpoint and edge infrastructure use cases including physical security, vehicle safety, telematics, autonomy, portable video, aerial drones, and other emerging robotic applications. Building on this footprint, Ambarella offers a full-stack edge AI platform, from highly optimized silicon and programmable software to AI agentic frameworks that coordinate perception, decision-making and control across devices. Ambarella’s low-power systems-on-chip (SoCs) integrate proprietary and highly efficient perception and deep learning neural network AI accelerators, enabling electronic systems to become more productive with partial or complete levels of machine autonomy. Memory supply shortages and rising component prices are disrupting customer demand, particularly within Ambarella’s consumer Internet of Things (IoT) business.

Memory Supply Constraints Disrupt Customer Orders Chief Executive Fermi Wang highlighted the worsening supply environment in the company’s earnings release, stating that “the unprecedented rise in memory prices and the scarcity of memory supply we previously highlighted has intensified and is causing many customers to reduce their outlooks,” with the consumer IoT segment particularly affected.
Customers have responded to the challenging supply conditions by cancelling, postponing or delaying orders, placing significant pressure on Ambarella’s near-term revenue outlook.

Get Started Ambarella Shares Plunge 37.5% as Revenue Miss and Weak Guidance Prompt Morgan Stanley Downgrade Fiona Craig NASDAQ:AMBA Latest News November 25 2026 6:00AM Add as preferred source © Adobe Stock Images Ambarella (NASDAQ:AMBA) shares fell 37.5% to $27.80 in premarket trading on Wednesday after the edge artificial intelligence semiconductor developer reported weaker-than-expected fiscal third-quarter revenue and issued fourth-quarter guidance significantly below analyst forecasts. The company expects fourth-quarter revenue of between $70 million and $75 million, representing a sequential decline of approximately 37% and falling well short of market expectations of around $112 million. Memory supply shortages and rising component prices are disrupting customer demand, particularly within Ambarella’s consumer Internet of Things (IoT) business. Memory Supply Constraints Disrupt Customer Orders Chief Executive Fermi Wang highlighted the worsening supply environment in the company’s earnings release, stating that “the unprecedented rise in memory prices and the scarcity of memory supply we previously highlighted has intensified and is causing many customers to reduce their outlooks,” with the consumer IoT segment particularly affected. Customers have responded to the challenging supply conditions by cancelling, postponing or delaying orders, placing significant pressure on Ambarella’s near-term revenue outlook. Despite these challenges, Wang maintained that the memory-related disruption does not alter the company’s long-term growth prospects in edge artificial intelligence. Revenue from edge AI products reached a record level during the third quarter. Morgan Stanley Downgrades Ambarella and Cuts Price Target Morgan Stanley downgraded Ambarella from Overweight to Equalweight on Wednesday, reducing its price target to $42 from $70. The investment bank cited significant near-term business disruption resulting from memory supply constraints, although it considers these challenges temporary. Morgan Stanley expects weakness in the consumer segment to continue through the January quarter and into the April quarter. The company’s enterprise and automotive businesses could also experience difficulties before conditions improve. Separately, insider transaction data indicated sustained net selling over the past 12 months, with no insider purchases recorded during the period. Semiconductor Sector Faces Broader Selling Pressure Ambarella’s decline comes amid wider weakness across semiconductor and technology stocks. The Nasdaq fell 1.9%, while the S&P 500 declined approximately 1%. The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index recorded a decline of around 7.9% overnight. Shares in major memory manufacturers Samsung and SK Hynix also fell sharply, despite the supply shortages affecting customers of downstream semiconductor developers such as Ambarella. The company reported adjusted earnings per share of $1.54, exceeding the consensus estimate of $1.52. Net sales increased 8.9% year-on-year to $1.67 billion, in line with market expectations. However, weaker growth at Anthropologie, rising operating costs and expectations of slower revenue growth during the fourth quarter weighed on investor sentiment. The performance lagged the company’s other major brands, with FP Group reporting comparable retail sales growth of 8.5% and the Urban Outfitters brand achieving growth of 5.8%. Management indicated that Anthropologie’s product transition was progressing more slowly than anticipated, contributing to expectations of higher markdown rates during the holiday shopping period. Fourth-Quarter Guidance Points to Slower Growth Urban Outfitters expects total company sales to increase at a mid-single-digit rate during the fourth quarter, representing a slowdown from the 8.9% growth achieved in the third quarter. Management also expects Anthropologie’s comparable sales to remain broadly unchanged during the holiday quarter. Additional pressure on profitability is expected from higher transportation costs. Fuel surcharges associated with the ongoing Middle East conflict are anticipated to reduce fourth-quarter gross margin by approximately 75 basis points. The downgrade reflected concerns surrounding the brand’s performance and the company’s near-term growth prospects.
